sections.domain: Impairment offenses and loss of driving privileges
sections.heading: Impairment offenses and loss of driving privileges
sections.markdown:
# Impairment offenses and loss of driving privileges

FACT_ID: sec15-R01 | anchor: A01
If another driver appears intoxicated, keep a substantial distance rather than trying to stop that vehicle yourself. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R02 | anchor: A01
Do not signal a suspected impaired driver to pull over. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R03 | anchor: A01
Record vehicle details or a plate number only if doing so does not compromise safety. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R04 | anchor: A01
Pull over before calling emergency services to report a suspected impaired driver’s description and location. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R05 | anchor: A01
Leave enforcement action against a suspected impaired motorist to police. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R06 | anchor: A01
A medicine or other drug can impair coordination or judgment and cause drowsiness. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R07 | anchor: A01
Combining drugs with alcohol can intensify impairment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R08 | anchor: A01
Over-the-counter and prescribed medicines can affect driving, so check the product’s warnings. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R09 | anchor: A01
The guide treats drug-impaired driving as subject to impaired-driving penalties as well as alcohol-impaired driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R10 | anchor: A01
Marijuana can affect vision, concentration and judging time, speed or distance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec15-R11 | anchor: A02
Criminally negligent or reckless vehicle operation is punishable conduct under the guide. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec15-R12 | anchor: A02
A driver involved in or causing a crash must stop, identify the driver and provide reasonable aid. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec15-R13 | anchor: A02
Knowingly refusing an officer’s signal to stop can constitute flight from an officer. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec15-R14 | anchor: A02
Implied consent is the guide’s term for consent to chemical testing associated with operating a vehicle on state highways. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec15-R15 | anchor: A02
The guide states that refusing an alcohol-analysis test can result in suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec15-R16 | anchor: A02
Chemical-test consequences depend on factors including age, measured alcohol level and previous offenses. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec15-R17 | anchor: A03
A DWI conviction is listed as a ground for suspending driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec15-R18 | anchor: A03
Failing to stop for a school bus boarding or unloading children is listed as a suspension ground. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec15-R19 | anchor: A03
Unlawful license use or concealing an important fact on a license application can result in suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec15-R20 | anchor: A03
Violating a license restriction or failing to answer a traffic charge can affect driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec15-R21 | anchor: A03
Failure to meet required financial-responsibility obligations can cause license suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec15-R22 | anchor: A03
Driving during a suspension can bring further penalties and extend the suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0132]

FACT_ID: sec15-R23 | anchor: A03
After a suspension period ends, the guide requires a reinstatement fee before driving privileges are restored. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0132]
